text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's parliament revised the 1996 budget for a second time this year to meet risisng interest payments on the country's domestic debt.
-- Bulgaria's National Price Commission had asked the cabinet to update fuel prices each week to avert losses from the fall in the lev, price commission said. @
The cabinet has so far revised fuel prices monthly or fortnightly in line with inflation and the lev/dollar exchange rate.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet shortlisted six foreign banks to advise the government in the planned sale of a 25 percent stake of the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company.
-- Bulgaria's First Private Bank whose insolvency was sought by the central bank (BNB) on May 31 has posted 20 billion levs pre-tax profit by November 30, BNB officials said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to approve on Monday a programme for the fast sale of 480 companies in 1997 with proceeds expected at some 43 billion levs.
-- Bulgaria is expected to import 70,000 tonnes of wheat from Syria under a debt-for-grain bilateral agreement, a Bulgarian government official said.
-- Some 4,000 criminals have been operating in organised street gangs in Bulgara during the last 3-4 years, Justice ministry figures showed. @

-- The Association of Bulgarian meat exporters to the European Union (EU) said they expected the temporary ban on exports of Bulgarian lamb meat to the EU to be lifted on Monday after an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in southeastern Bulgaria was eliminated in November. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
